chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, all from Al-A'ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) had me read something from the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), and it contained: 'You are forbidden from the catfish, the glyptothorax, the sea horse, the floating fish, and the spleen.' I said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah have mercy on you, fish without scales are brought to us.' He said, 'Eat what has scales from the fish, and do not eat what does not have scales.'

key_terms.الطَّافِي: Floating fish (often referring to dead or scaleless varieties)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for eating fish in Shia jurisprudence according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of the Four Scholars, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the general principle of fish consumption by linking permissibility to the presence of scales ('qishr'), resolving the ambiguity of species like catfish. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between halal and haram aquatic creatures, emphasizing the Prophet's family's authority in interpreting dietary laws beyond the explicit Quranic mentions.
